lines.text: You can take {G} off {WHEN}. Bring an extra layer to wear with {GP} {WHEN2}. || It opens with a compliment and ends with 'no offense, but.'
Take {G} off {WHEN}, then put {GP} back on {WHEN2} with an extra layer on top. || Today is a cat. Warm and friendly, then the claws.
{G} can come off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || The cold never leaves. It just steps out to take a call.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || The heat isn't leaving. It's moving to a slightly smaller apartment.
Some relief from the heat {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || The weather turns the oven off. It leaves the door shut.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || Someone will call it 'cooling down' while fanning themselves with a menu.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || The snow's doing what TV shows do now: releasing in two parts.
The snow stops for a while later, then comes back {WHENP}. || Normal snow service resumes after the break. We apologize for the convenience.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || It snows the way printers print. Some, a pause that means nothing, then more.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || Scheduled maintenance on the sky. Expect brief leaks.
There's a short rain shower {WHENP}. Have the umbrella with you. || Like a toddler with a garden hose: brief, random, and very pleased with itself.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || The sky's reply-all. Short, unnecessary, and everyone gets it.
A rain shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || Somebody left their car windows down. This shower knows which car.
This works for the rest of the night. || Out there, it's down to delivery drivers and bad decisions.
You're dressed right for the rest of the night. || The weather saves its drama for daytime, when there's an audience.
This works for the rest of the night. || The rest of the night fits on a sticky note. I used a whole screen anyway.
The rain stops later, but bring the umbrella for now. || Afterwards, everything out there smells fresh. You'll have to manage that yourself.
Later the rain stops. For now, keep the umbrella with you. || When it stops, people come out smiling. Then you come out.
The rain stops later, but bring the umbrella for now. || Of everyone I forecast for, you're the one I'd let get rained on.
The snow stops later. || Make a snow angel after, if you want. Yours always look like a crime-scene outline.
It keeps snowing for a while, then stops. || Snowflakes look romantic in most people's hair. In yours, they look like dandruff.
It keeps snowing for a while, then stops. || Snow sticks to everything it lands on. It slides right off you.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP}. || Out in it after, you'll look like the 'before' picture in a coat ad.
The snow stops for a while later, then comes back {WHENP}. || The only thing that ever comes back for you.
It snows for now, takes a break, and starts again {WHENP}. || In the break, you'll look out and say 'that's it?' People say that about you too.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP} and starts again {WHENP}. || That's two rounds of you saying 'it's really coming down.' Nobody needed one.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || Snow builds up on anything that doesn't move. You'll want to watch that.
Pack the umbrella. Rain sets in {WHENP} and doesn't let up. || You'll drip into every doorway like a golden retriever. Minus the charm.
Rain arrives {WHENP} and stays, so take the umbrella. || Wet cats get millions of views online. Don't get your hopes up.
It starts raining {WHENP} and keeps going, so bring the umbrella. || A big day for snails and mushrooms. You've always had a lot in common.
{WHENP} the rain sets in for good. Bring the umbrella. || Everyone will be avoiding the rain. It'll find out what being you is like.
You can take the winter coat off {WHEN}. || Pulling it off will give you a static shock. The most spark you'll show all day.
{WHEN} you can do without the winter coat. || Public notice: you'll be out in your regular clothes. We apologize in advance.
{WHEN} it's warm enough to lose the winter coat. || Out of it, you'll look like a hot dog without the bun. Nobody orders that.
You can take the winter coat off {WHEN}. || You'll feel ten pounds lighter. You won't look it.
Later, kids everywhere get zipped into something against their will.
Later the park benches go cold. People find out by sitting down.
The cold waits until people are too far from home to turn back. It's done this before.
Somewhere an office opens a window for the warm part. Nobody will agree on when to close it.
The weather takes a layer off just to see who copies it.
The warm part was not a promise. The weather's lawyer asked me to say that.
The rain always picks the moment someone's carrying groceries in both arms.
Somewhere, white sneakers are having their last good day.
Every umbrella gets shaken out at a door, all over whoever's behind it.
I drew you warmer later. I also drew you taller. Artistic license.
Later the layer comes off. Turns out the tired look goes all the way down.
Later it warms up. You'll roll up your sleeves like you're about to do something.
Later you'll go almost a whole minute without complaining. A personal best.
Strangers share umbrellas with the cute people first. Bring your own.
You'll say 'I actually like rain' to sound interesting. It didn't work last time either.
Rain's supposed to be good for the skin. It'll do what it can.
Later it cools off. Management has been informed and does not care.
Later it cools off. Not by much. Just enough to be petty about it.
Later it cools off. Every hand out there goes into a pocket, like they're all hiding something.
Warm, then cold again. Please keep all layers with you until the ride comes to a complete stop.
Warm, then cold again. A day built by someone who's never had to dress for it.
Warm, then cold again. Expect a big rise in people saying 'it's deceiving out there.'
Warm, then cold again. Every toddler in town gets wrestled out of a jacket and back into it, screaming both times.
Later it warms up. The cold is being let go. No severance.
Later it warms up. Hats come off all over town. Brace for the hair.
Later it warms up. The weather started cold just to make the rest look generous.
Everyone out there will do that fast walk that refuses to be called running.
Every umbrella out there will be held at exactly someone else's eye level.
Big day for the man who refuses to own an umbrella. He's proving a point to nobody.
Warm, then cold again. The weather will be nice to you for a while, then remember who you are.
Warm, then cold again. You'll warm up for a while. Longer than your last hobby lasted.
Warm, then cold again. You'll overheat in the middle and turn the color of a ham.
Warm, then cold again. A day like this needs someone flexible. You can't even touch your toes.
Warm, then cold again. You'll spend the day fiddling with a zipper. Easily your most skilled work this week.
A T-shirt day. Probably the free one from that fun run you mostly walked.
A T-shirt day. You'll stand outside with your face up like a lizard with a mortgage.
A T-shirt day. If your shirt has words on it, it'll be the wittiest thing about you.
A T-shirt day. You'll catch your reflection in a store window and speed up.
Later it warms up. The weather gets a second act. You're still waiting on your first.
Later it warms up. You'll warm up too, eventually. People usually leave before that.
Later it warms up. You'll step outside and blink like you've just been released.
Later it warms up. You'll thaw out in stages, like a supermarket chicken.
